scope: Use a reported DWG-to-DXF interoperability case to refine how strict parse, recovery/audit, reduced output, and preservation evidence are graded.

method.kind: Primary project issue/docs review plus local plan cross-check
localInspection: DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md: existing writer-output, strict-versus-recovery, semantic inventory, and fixture-admission gates
method.limitations: Issue #1136 is a historical reporter/maintainer discussion involving LibreDWG 0.13.3 and ezdxf 1.3.2, with attachments not downloaded or independently rerun. Later comments report an ezdxf reader change and hundreds of audit/recovery fixes, but do not establish current peer behavior or a local libdxfrw defect.

evidence.topic: Full and reduced output modes have distinct preservation outcomes
observed: Autodesk's BLOCK reference lists group 2 as the block name, and its BLOCKS example includes the name in each BLOCK record.
The report says a full LibreDWG dwg2dxf R2004 output failed ezdxf strict parsing and initially also failed ezdxf recovery because a BLOCK was missing required group 2 name data.
The reporter says the reduced (-m) output parsed but stripped information.

The issue later records an ezdxf reader change, a LibreDWG audit reporting 322 repairs, and a BricsCAD recovery report of 320 repairs; the comment says saving requires recovery to make the document valid.
The thread was closed after the ezdxf reader change; this does not show a LibreDWG output correction or current cross-version acceptance.
doesNotEstablish: A reproducible current peer defect because the files and exact binaries were not pinned or rerun.
A libdxfrw defect or any local runtime behavior.
Semantic preservation from the reduced output's parse success.
A zero audit count as a full graph or semantic-completeness oracle.
evidence.planUse: Keep full and reduced writer modes separate, bind outputs to the same local source manifest, and record strict parse, recovery/audit changes, and semantic deltas as separate outcomes.

evidence.topic: Strict read, recovery, audit, and valid save/reopen are different states
observed: ezdxf documentation recommends ordinary readfile for trusted files and recover.readfile for flawed inputs; recovery returns an auditor and can leave errors.
Issue #1136 illustrates that recovery initially could not load a missing-name BLOCK, and later comments distinguish loading from repairing the document for save.
doesNotEstablish: That ezdxf is a normative validator for every DXF profile.
That any recovered model is safe to save or semantically equivalent without checking its fixes and errors.
evidence.planUse: Label strict parse, recovered parse, audit fixes/errors, and strict reopen of recovered output separately; do not count recovery success alone as writer acceptance.

readinessRefinement: At the composed peer checkpoint, run full and reduced output modes separately and compare both to the same source-authored manifest.
Record exact peer version/command/output hash, strict parse outcome, recovery/audit fixes and errors, save/reopen result, and semantic identity/owner/payload delta.
Treat a reduced output that parses as a lossy-profile observation only; it cannot promote full writer preservation.
Keep peer/native work out of the per-slice loop; use existing generated fast writer/readback checks and fixture policy.
